decisions.title: Store money as integer minor units
decisions.summary: All amounts are stored and computed as integer minor units (cents) with an explicit currency code.
decisions.body:
## Context
Float storage produced off-by-one-cent differences between the ledger and bank statements.

## Decision
Use `BIGINT` minor units plus a three-letter `currency` column. Convert only at the API edge.

## Consequences
Every amount needs a currency. Division (splits, fees) must use the shared rounding helper.

## Alternatives
Decimal columns: exact, but slower in our reporting queries and awkward in JavaScript.

memories.title: Payment provider sends amounts as strings
memories.summary: Webhook payloads carry amounts as decimal strings like "12.50"; parse them, never cast to float.
memories.body:
The provider's webhook JSON uses strings for amounts, with two decimals for most currencies and none for zero-decimal ones.

We found this when a `parseFloat` turned "0.29" into 28 minor units. Verify with the sample payloads in `test/webhooks/samples/`.

memories.title: Monthly reports must reconcile to the cent
memories.summary: Finance rejects any monthly report whose totals differ from bank statements by even one minor unit.
memories.body:
Report totals are compared against bank statements exactly; there is no tolerance.

Source: the finance review notes for September. Check by running the reconciliation script against the last closed month.
